_doc: M1's motion instructions, rewritten. The graph's own motion field carries the same lamp-flame sentence on all fourteen generate shots and animates none of the film's beats - PRODUCTION_ORDERS calls for the 89 to be rewritten and these are M1's fourteen. data/ is untouched.
_shape: Every instruction says three things in this order: the beat, what does NOT move, and the ambient life last and smallest. The order is deliberate - the beat first because it is the shot, the negative second because reference-conditioned video will invent a camera move if nobody forbids one, and the ambient last because it is the least important thing in the frame and a prompt weights what it says first.
_camera: The pack marks all sixteen shots `locked`. Every instruction says the camera does not move, in words, every time.
_must_not_drift: The pack: 'the king's costume from 04 onward; the sage's seated posture from 07.' Both are named in the shots they govern.
_approved_by: the action list accepted by Venkat, 2026-09-22, with the sage's nod cut from 01-06 and 01-09 and 01-11 kept as small hand moves

01-01.instruction: An empty hall in morning light. Nothing enters and no one appears. The only movement is dust turning slowly in the shafts of lattice light, and one lamp flame drifting. The camera does not move. The walls, floor, pillars and light do not change.

01-02.instruction: The sage walks away from the camera, up the hall toward the distant dais, seen from behind. An unhurried walk, staff planted with each second step, his draped cloth swinging and settling as he goes. The seated ministers on both sides stay still and do not turn. The camera does not move. The hall, the pillars and the light do not change.

01-03.instruction: Seated ministers turn their heads toward the entrance, one after another, unhurried - curiosity, not alarm. Nobody stands. Nobody speaks. Their draped cloth settles as they turn. The camera does not move. The hall and the light do not change.
01-03._why: Re-rendered on 2026-09-23 from a new still with the foreground diya removed, so there is no flame in the shot to come loose. The instruction is unchanged.

01-04.instruction: The seated king leans forward and BEGINS to rise, lifting a little - he does not complete the stand and does not reach his full height. The crown is rigid. It is fixed on his head and moves exactly with it. Its shape, size and ornament never change. His draped cloth shifts a little as he leans. His face, necklaces and armbands do not change. Nobody else moves. The camera does not move.
01-04._why: Re-written by the director on 2026-09-23. The first clip floated the crown: it stayed at the same height while his head rose under it, and its silhouette changed across the shot. Two changes - the crown is stated as a rigid object fixed to the head, and the movement is made smaller, because a smaller move gives the model less to redraw. The window is chosen for the LEAST crown deformation rather than the most movement; `kind: stable` selects that.

01-05.instruction: The king walks down the steps of the dais, one step at a time, opening his arms as he comes. His draped cloth moves with each step and settles. His crown, ornament, costume and face do not change. Nobody else moves. The camera does not move. The hall and the light do not change.

01-06.instruction: Water pours in a steady stream from a vessel over a pair of bare feet on stone, splashing and running away across the floor. Hands hold the vessel and tilt it. No face is visible and none enters the frame. The camera does not move. Nothing else in the frame changes.

01-07.instruction: Two men seated facing each other on the same level, both still. The king's head inclines very slightly as he asks. The sage does not move; his seated posture does not change. The empty throne behind them does not change. The only other movement is a lamp flame drifting and draped cloth settling. The camera does not move.

01-08.instruction: The sage waits, seated, and does not answer. His seated posture does not change and his hands do not move. The smallest life only: breath, one lamp flame drifting, draped cloth settling. The camera does not move.

01-09.instruction: The king, seated, opens one hand a small distance - an easy, unthinking, generous gesture, no larger than a hand's width. Nothing else about him moves; his crown, ornament, costume and face do not change. The camera does not move. A lamp flame drifts.

01-10.instruction: Ministers seated along the hall, watching, attentive and at ease. Nobody is troubled and nobody reacts. Almost no movement at all: breath, a lamp flame drifting, draped cloth settling. The camera does not move.

01-11.instruction: The king lifts one hand a small distance, palm opening upward, level and unforced - a small movement, no larger than a hand's width, and it stops. Nothing else about him moves; his crown, ornament, costume and face do not change. The camera does not move. A lamp flame drifts.

01-12.instruction: A pair of open hands resting on knees, palms up, completely unchanged. The fingers do not close and do not move. No face is visible. The only movement is draped cloth settling and the light shifting very slightly. The camera does not move.

01-13.instruction: A man's face at ease, almost pleased, held nearly still. Breath only, and one slow blink. His crown, ornament and costume do not change. The camera does not move. A lamp flame drifts behind him.

01-14.instruction: The sage's face, about to speak: the smallest intake of breath, his lips parting slightly, and it stops there. He does not speak. His seated posture does not change. The camera does not move. A lamp flame drifts.

_no_motion.01-15: motion_allowed: false - a reuse of 01-13. Nothing is animated.
_no_motion.01-16: motion_allowed: false - a reuse of 01-14, and the film's final hold. Nothing is animated.

standing_rules: Flames stay on their wicks. They may flicker in place; they never slide, drift, detach, multiply or change count.
No new flame, lamp, fire or glowing light appears anywhere in the frame. Nothing burns that is not already burning in the first frame.
_standing_rules_why: A standing rule is appended to EVERY instruction this file sends, by tools/motion_film.js, rather than pasted into each one by hand - a rule that has to be remembered fourteen times is a rule that will be forgotten once. The flame rule was set by the director on 2026-09-23 after M1's first motion pass: a generative video model does not know a flame is attached to a wick, and in 01-03 the diya's flames slid along the rim and one detached. The three shots already made were fixed by freezing (direction/m1-flame-freeze.json); this is so the next one does not need fixing. A second rule was added on 2026-09-23. The first rule tells a flame to stay on its wick and says nothing about a flame that never had one: 01-09 came back with a large flame the model INVENTED, floating free in mid-air against the steps with nothing holding it, changing shape across the whole shot. It is not in the approved still. A rule against drifting cannot catch a flame that was never there to drift.
